newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria faces petrol crisis, refinery lacks oil.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria faces petrol crisis, refinery lacks oil.

text.p: Debt-ridden Bulgaria, shaken by nation-wide strikes and protests, will face a severe petrol crisis this week with its biggest oil refinery running out of crude, officials said on Tuesday.
They said the state-owned Neftohim refinery, which normally feeds more than 70 percent of the domestic market, had only 26,400 tonnes of crude in stock.
The Bourgas plant's management was desperately awaiting the arrival of a delayed 72,000-tonne crude tanker, named Osam, from Russia's port of Odessa.
A senior plant official, who declined to be named, said one atmosphere distillation unit at the refinery has been closed and another one -- AD-4 was on the edge of its minimum.
"Since yesterday we are refining just 8,000 tonnes of crude per day," plant spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said by telephone. Last week the plant refined 16,000 tonnes of crude per day, she added.
On Tuesday some petrol stations in the country lacked all kinds of petrol. Sofia residents were queueing to stockpile petrol remembering a severe shortage in 1990.
Russia's Rosneft said on Tuesday that it had cut crude oil supplies to Neftohim because of unpaid debts.

Bulgaria is without an effective government since December 21 when the Socialist cabinet of Zhan Videnov resigned. Nation-wide protests escalated to a general strike demanding immediate general elections.

Trade union leaders at Bourgas refinery, where protesters blocked the plant's exits and its terminal for an hour to stop fuel going to the country, have decided to shut down the plant completely from Wednesday.
Rosneft, the Russian state-owned oil company that is being privatised, supplies oil directly to the refinery through its Rosbulneft joint venture with Neftohim.

Valentin Zlatev, head of Rosneft's export department, said only one 70,000-tonne vessel of oil had gone to Neftohim in January out of a planned four, and that future deliveries were in question until debts were repaid.

Trade union officials at Neftohim said the plant owed millions of dollars to suppliers, many of whom were no longer delivering. The plant had losses of some 100 billion levs last year and 37 billion levs in January, they added.
